title: ADP qualification config
description: Bounded qualification configuration for tests/e2e/orchestration. Documents the contract enforced by config.py, which is the authority: the loader is hand-written (the repo-root test tree has no jsonschema dependency) and enforces rules this schema cannot express, notably the embedded-secret scan and the refusal of production targets. Keep the two in sync when either changes.

config_version.description: Layout version. A different value is refused rather than guessed at.

environment.description: Target environment. 'prod'/'production' are refused: this harness provisions fixtures.

connection_ref.description: Registered user connection to run through. Never a credential. Resolved through the connection registry before run, resume and cleanup: an unregistered, revoked or unresolvable ref refuses the mutation, and the registry's account/org must match the expected_* fields below.

expected_account_id.description: The AWS account the selected connection is expected to resolve to. Checked against BOTH the connection registry's authoritative account and sts:GetCallerIdentity before run, resume and cleanup; any disagreement, or an unreadable identity, refuses the mutation. The registry is the authority — this field only declares what the config believes, so drift is caught rather than trusted. A string, not a number, so a leading zero survives.

expected_org.description: The GitHub org the authorized repository must belong to. Checked against the owner segment of 'repository' and against the registered connection's org.

identity.description: References to org/team/identity fixtures. References only; this harness does not duplicate the production identity APIs.

versions.description: Pinned versions. An exact semver or a 40-character commit SHA; floating refs such as 'latest' or 'main' are refused so a qualification is reproducible.

bounds.description: Every bound is required and must be positive. Ceilings are additionally enforced by config.py (BOUND_CEILINGS) so a typo cannot authorize a large spend.

max_resources.description: Maximum fixtures that may exist at once, counting unresolved ones.

max_usd.description: Spend ceiling in USD. Does not replace the policy/budget authority in #5128.

directory.description: Where inventories and evidence are written. May not contain '..' segments.

secret_refs.description: Named REFERENCES to credentials, resolved at runtime only. A literal credential here is refused, as is a secret-like key anywhere else in this file.

scenarios.description: Scenario adapter ids to run, supplied by #5157. Empty or absent means all registered adapters; an id with no registered adapter is an error, not a smaller run.
